title: Box geometry parity on off-grid positions — preview bounds vs the emitted command
threshold: identity: every row's box must be the SAME output pixel (exact integer equality on x/y/width/height) AND its raw corner residual must stay under 1e-09px; exceptions must be 0 (L-Q11)

instrumentChange.what: the verdict was `maxCornerDeltaPx != 0.0`; it is now exact-integer pixel identity plus a 1e-9px ceiling on the raw residual
instrumentChange.why: The preview holds its box normalised (DD-2 — the only space a display-sized canvas and a 1920x1080 export can share). Recovering the pixel is `n/W*W`, which in float64 is not always `n`: 770/1080*1080 is 769.9999999999999. `!= 0.0` therefore stopped measuring geometry below ~1e-12px and started measuring which integers survive a binary round-trip — it read 0 exceptions before the origin was snapped to the even grid and 33 after, with both runs describing the same box.
instrumentChange.notAThresholdRelaxation: The geometric quantity is EXACTLY equal on every row: both sides are the same integer, and production rebuilds it with Math.round (CanvasCompositor._drawImageLayer), so it recovers that integer. The new predicate is strictly stronger where it matters — nothing within half a pixel passes — and the raw residual is still reported per row. The sensitivity mutation is judged by this same predicate and still fails it.

method: Preview: buildImageLayersAt(items, t, undefined, 853/480, exportFrame).bounds, multiplied by the output resolution exactly as _drawImageLayer does. Export: the scale=/overlay= integers parsed back out of the filtergraph that rendered a real file through _process_image_overlays. Neither is recomputed here.
unquantisedBaselineNote: legacyPreviewBoxPx is the SAME production function called without an exportFrame — i.e. the B0 behaviour. It is reported per row so the size of what this round fixed is visible, not asserted.

sensitivity.detectedBy: the pixelIdentical predicate — the same one the verdict uses, so this proves the verdict can fail rather than proving some looser reading can
